ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — History and Physical — Higuchi Ichiyō — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: New patient visit for seven weeks of cough, fevers, night sweats and weight loss: chest X-ray, sputum specimens, blood tests, airborne precautions, and a report of suspected tuberculosis to the public health center

text.paragraph: New patient visit for seven weeks of cough, fevers, night sweats and weight loss: chest X-ray, sputum specimens, blood tests, airborne precautions, and a report of suspected tuberculosis to the public health center [S]
This fictional modern episode addresses the presenting concerns below. [S]

list.item: She has coughed for weeks, sweats at night and has lost weight, and fears it is tuberculosis. [S]
She supports her household by writing and cannot afford to stop working or to pay for many tests. [S]
She is afraid of passing the illness to the people she lives with and of what neighbors and editors will think. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Higuchi Ichiyō, whose given name was Natsu (also written Natsuko), was born in Tokyo on the 25th day of the 3rd month of Meiji 5 in the Japanese lunisolar calendar, which is 2 May 1872 in the Gregorian calendar, in official housing within the grounds of the Tokyo prefectural office in Uchisaiwai-chō (now in Chiyoda). [D]

Japan replaced its lunisolar calendar with the Gregorian calendar at the end of Meiji 5: the 3rd day of the 12th month of Meiji 5 became 1 January 1873 (Meiji 6). Dates before then, including her birth, were recorded in the old calendar. [D]
From 1886 she studied classical poetry (waka) at the Haginoya academy of Nakajima Utako. [D]

Her father died of illness in the summer of 1889, when she was 17, leaving debts from a failed business; she became head of the household and took on the support of her mother and younger sister, who did washing and needlework, and the family lived in poverty. [D]

In 1891 she became a pupil of the novelist Nakarai Tōsui and began to write fiction, choosing to earn her living by writing at a time when this was very hard for a woman; her story Umoregi (1892) brought her into the literary world. [D]

From July 1893 to April 1894 she ran a small shop selling household goods and cheap sweets in Shitaya Ryūsenji-chō, beside the Yoshiwara pleasure quarter (now in Taitō); the shop closed after about ten months, and her life there became material for Takekurabe. [D]
In May 1894 she moved to Hongō Maruyama-Fukuyama-chō (now Nishikata, Bunkyō). [D]

At Maruyama-Fukuyama-chō she wrote the works that made her name, among them Ōtsugomori (1894), Nigorie (1895), Takekurabe (1895 to 1896) and Jūsan'ya; Nippon.com calls the period 'the miraculous 14 months', and the Nipponica encyclopedia calls the time up to January 1896 'the miraculous year'. [D]
From the beginning of 1896 her health declined rapidly. [D]

text.paragraph: 3 later historical claims are omitted because they describe events after the index age. See the teaching note.
Historical biography with true dates. These events are not part of the synthetic care timeline.
No historical medical events are recorded.

list.item: Writer of short fiction and essays, paid by the piece by literary magazines; writes at home at a low desk, mostly at night; finished several stories in the past year and is working on new ones with editors waiting [S]

Head of a household of three adults in a small rented house in Hongō, Tokyo; provides for the household from her writing income, which is low and irregular, with unpaid bills; enrolled in National Health Insurance [S]
Never smoked; no alcohol (AUDIT-C 0); no drug use; no travel outside Japan; no incarceration, homelessness or work in health care; not sexually active [S]
Meals irregular and small, mostly rice, pickles and tea, with fish or tofu a few times a week when money allows [S]
Supports and strengths she names: her writing, her readers and editors, and the poetry she studied when young [S]

text.paragraph: No medications started by this date.

Positive for the concerns in the history of present illness. Alert, composed and precise in her answers, with a wry humor; thin and tired; organized thought. Mood worried about money, her household and her deadlines; PHQ-9 8, with item 9 scored 0; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. No other systems reported as affected in this synthetic episode. [S]

S — Synthetic presenting problem at intake, superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit; its timing echoes her documented decline from early 1896 (D).

list.item: Cough for about seven weeks with evening fevers, night sweats, poor appetite and weight loss of about 4 kg (about 10 percent) in a woman of 23; chest X-ray with patchy right upper lobe opacities and no cavity; suspected pulmonary tuberculosis; airborne precautions and three sputum specimens for acid-fast smear, nucleic acid amplification and culture: active, confirmed [S]
Moderate protein-calorie malnutrition: BMI 17.6, about 10 percent weight loss in two months, and albumin 3.3 g/dL: active, confirmed [S]
Low and irregular income from writing, with a household to support; costs of care are a barrier: active, confirmed [S]

Diagnosis and safety: chest X-ray; three sputum specimens at least eight hours apart, one early in the morning, for acid-fast smear, Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, liquid and solid culture and drug susceptibility testing; HIV, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests and a pregnancy test; blood count, liver and kidney tests, glucose and hemoglobin A1c; visual acuity and color vision before ethambutol. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 4: treatment: drug-susceptible tuberculosis treatment (2022); Official American Thoracic Society/Infectious Diseases Society of America/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Clinical Practice Guidelines: Diagnosis of Tuberculosis in Adults and Children (2017) [S]

Infectious diseases consultation at the results visit to confirm the diagnosis, choose between the six-month and four-month regimens, set the doses for her weight, and plan monitoring and infection control. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Updates on the Treatment of Drug-Susceptible and Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis: An Official ATS/CDC/ERS/IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline (2025); Interim Guidance: 4-Month Rifapentine-Moxifloxacin Regimen for the Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Pulmonary Tuberculosis - United States, 2022 (2022) [S]

Infection control and public health: airborne precautions in the clinic; at home, no visitors, a surgical mask in shared rooms, windows open, and sleeping in her own room until the public health center confirms she is no longer infectious; report of suspected tuberculosis to the public health center the same day and notification at once on diagnosis; a contact investigation of her household and other close contacts led by the public health center. Guideline: Official American Thoracic Society/Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Infectious Diseases Society of America Clinical Practice Guidelines: Treatment of Drug-Susceptible Tuberculosis (2016); Guidelines for the investigation of contacts of persons with infectious tuberculosis: recommendations from the National Tuberculosis Controllers Association and CDC (2005); 結核 (Tuberculosis): notification criteria under Article 12 of the Infectious Diseases Control Law (current) [S]

Nutrition, income and writing: two dietitian visits in the first month, three meals and two energy-dense snacks a day with two oral nutrition supplement drinks, and weight at every visit; a medical social worker to apply for public funding of tuberculosis treatment and to review other help with costs; a paced writing plan of short sessions in daylight with rest; PHQ-9 at intake, at two months and at the end of treatment. Guideline: 結核医療費の公費負担 (Public funding of tuberculosis medical costs under Articles 37 and 37-2 of the Infectious Diseases Control Law) (current); Consensus statement: Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and American Society for Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition: characteristics recommended for the identification and documentation of adult malnutrition (undernutrition) (2012); Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: Screening (2023) [S]
Referral to infectious diseases (tuberculosis), Hiroshi Abernathy-Okoye, MD, ordered 1896-04-14 [S]
